chapter_title: Chương 290: Hàn Quốc muốn bôi nhọ Tương Lai Kỷ Nguyên

segments.title: Chương 290: Hàn Quốc muốn bôi nhọ Tương Lai Kỷ Nguyên
segments.content:
Tencent's top executives received the news after the Spring Festival.

Pony Ma took the prospect of distributing "DNF" very seriously, personally checking in on it from time to time, and now he had urgently convened a meeting of the Interactive Entertainment Group.

Last year, Tencent had bought back stocks and reorganized internally.

While adjusting departments, they also brought in a large amount of fresh blood, and Pony Ma's control over the company reached a new height.

Most of the heads of the gaming department present at the meeting had been promoted or recruited from outside last year, and some had even officially joined during this year's Spring Festival.

Ren Yuxin, president of the gaming business, was a Tencent veteran.

The vice president, however, was Ma Xiaotie, who had only joined this month. Last year, he was still at G-Optics, and he was the one who had brought in "The Legend of Mir 3."

There was also a foreigner who was a gaming vice president, mainly responsible for building the technical platform.

Yao Xiaoguang, who would later create "Honor of Kings," had also joined Tencent last August, responsible for "imitating" popular casual games for in-house development. Tencent had spent a year and a half persuading him to join.

Of course, the person truly in charge of in-house development was Wang Bo. He was the one who created the QQ Game Hall, and he also led the development of "QQ Fantasy."

"Last year, 'QQ Fantasy' had a peak concurrent user count of over 600,000. Before the Spring Festival, it dropped to 230,000. Even with promotions during the festival, we only managed to bring the peak concurrent users back up to 310,000. I'm not saying there's a problem with the game's content, but the operations definitely have many issues..."

Ma Xiaotie, who had been in his new post for only a few days, was firing shots at the previous operations team.

Some of the veterans wore cold smiles, thinking to themselves: You nearly ran G-Optics into the ground, and now you dare to come here and spout nonsense? No matter how crappy the operations for "QQ Fantasy" are, can they be worse than "The Legend of Mir 3"?

A person who had done a terrible job with his original business was poached with a high salary to be airdropped in as the gaming vice president. One can imagine how many people were unconvinced.

In fact, Ma Xiaotie felt wronged himself. It was true that he had brought in "The Legend of Mir 3." But the game had become a huge hit before it even launched, and someone else came to pluck the fruit not long after he took charge. He had no control over how "The Legend of Mir 3" was operated.

Everyone discussed a whole host of issues at the meeting.

Finally, Ren Yuxin, the president of the gaming division, stood up and played two video clips on the projection screen. "This is gameplay footage from Korea's 'DNF,' and this is gameplay footage from Youke's 'Future Era.' As you can see, although the two games have completely different stories and graphics, their core gameplay is strikingly similar. Even some of the character classes are similar..."

Ren Yuxin continued, "I spent 10,000 yuan to buy a closed beta account from a player and personally played 'Future Era' for two whole days. I've also played 'DNF' myself. To be honest, whether comparing the game's world-building, story, graphics, or balance, 'Future Era' is a cut above 'DNF' in every aspect."

Pony Ma was silent for a long time before speaking, "So you're saying there's no need to distribute 'DNF'?"

Ren Yuxin shook his head. "Absolutely no need. But there's still a sliver of hope, and that is to immediately negotiate the distribution deal and complete the technical handover as quickly as possible. We should aim to launch 'DNF' within four months. After all, 'Future Era' has only completed the novice village part, and there are currently only a thousand players in the closed beta."

Yao Xiaoguang asked, "Did 'Future Era' really spend a year and eight months just to finish the novice village?"

Ren Yuxin said with a smile, "How is that possible? Based on the time the project lead for 'Future Era' left his previous job, this game has been in development for a year and one month at most. When you poach someone, they can't start working immediately. He still had to build a development team. I estimate the actual development time is less than a year."

"Even if it's only been a year, just making a novice village is still outrageous," Yao Xiaoguang said.

Why did Tencent spend a year and a half poaching Yao Xiaoguang? Because he was the developer of China's first 3D MMORPG, "Miracle."

Ren Yuxin continued, "There are two difficulties in launching 'DNF' before 'Future Era.' First, it's hard to complete the negotiations and technical handover quickly. Second, even if we succeed, the game's quality won't compare, and it's highly likely we'll lose money."

Pony Ma knew him well. "Tell me what you're really thinking."

Ren Yuxin said, "When 'Future Era' was first being planned, Chen Guiliang most likely had never seen 'DNF.' But the core gameplay of the two games is so similar, I suspect that during the development of 'Future Era,' they must have borrowed game ideas from 'DNF.' If Youke can develop it in-house, why can't we? A side-scrolling fighting online game could absolutely become a brand new game genre, just like MMOs."

"Is it too late to start in-house development now?" Ma Xiaotie asked.

Ren Yuxin smiled. "For any type of online game, some come out first, some later. It's not a question of being early or late, but whether the game's quality and operational strategy are excellent."

Pony Ma considered it carefully, then started assigning tasks, "Yao Xiaoguang will be in charge of developing this type of game in-house. He has experience developing large-scale games, and he has been successful."

Having received his orders, Yao Xiaoguang suggested, "'DNF' and 'Future Era' are both 2D. We can develop the new game in 3D. This way, we'll be innovating and can bring a brand new experience to players. Also, the world-building and story of 'Future Era' are just too impressive. I hope to recruit the best literature planners. It would be even better if we could directly adapt a popular novel."

"'Ghost Blows Out the Light' is quite popular," someone suggested.

Pony Ma asked, "From the name, it sounds like a horror story?"

The person replied, "You can think of it as a Chinese version of 'Indiana Jones,' but with a lot of Chinese feng shui, history, and tomb-raiding elements. The book is being serialized on Qidian."

Ren Yuxin shook his head. "Qidian was acquired by Shanda long ago. They won't sell the game adaptation rights."

Indeed, they wouldn't sell.

When Chen Guiliang sent people to buy the rights, Qidian would only sell the physical publishing rights and film adaptation rights. As for the game rights for "Ghost Blows Out the Light," Qidian absolutely refused to sell them.

Pony Ma said, "Then we'll write our own game story."

Yao Xiaoguang added, "If I take on this project, I hope I won't be rushed to meet deadlines."

Someone joked, "Are you also planning to take a year and eight months to make the novice village?"

"It definitely won't be that slow. But to make a high-quality 3D game, one year is certainly not enough. It will take at least a year and a half to two years or more," Yao Xiaoguang said.

And so, the matter was settled. Tencent switched from its original plan of distributing "DNF" to developing its own 3D side-scrolling fighting online game.

After the meeting, Pony Ma took out his phone and realized he didn't have Chen Guiliang's number saved.

He had his assistant contact Chen Guiliang's secretary and finally got through to Chen Guiliang on the phone. "Do you still want a five-digit QQ number?"

"Yes, I do," Chen Guiliang said.

Pony Ma asked casually, "When will 'Future Era' open for registration?"

"Summer vacation," Chen Guiliang answered without hiding anything, as this news was about to be announced.

Pony Ma left it at that and said no more.

Luckily, "Future Era" was being tested now. Otherwise, if they had waited until Tencent had secured the distribution rights for "DNF," Tencent would have been in deep trouble.

In reality, how could Chen Guiliang afford to wait?

By the time Tencent finalized the distribution agreement for "DNF," it was already December 2007. It's ridiculous for a game distribution deal to take a year and a half to negotiate. The Korean developers were quite something. Even "World of Warcraft" wasn't that much of a hassle.

Compared to Pony Ma's composure, Chen Tianqiao had been tearing his hair out for the past year.

Although he made it onto the "Forbes China Rich List" last year, Forbes only reported his assets at 3.3 billion.

That's because Shanda's stock price plummeted by 70% last year!

The reason for the stock price drop was the switch of games like "The Legend of Mir" to a free-to-play model. The transition from pay-to-play to free-to-play caused a sharp decline in Shanda's revenue in a short period, scaring investors into selling off their stocks.

Although Shanda quickly recovered its earnings, news then broke that the Shanda Box had failed.

The business concept of the Shanda Box was very advanced, but it was too advanced. It would have been more suitable to do it ten years later.

Almost all the company's senior executives opposed the Shanda Box project.

But Chen Tianqiao was overconfident, believing he was the only one who was right. He even enjoyed the process of being opposed by everyone, feeling a bit like "the whole world is drunk, but I alone am sober."

In February of last year, pre-orders for the Shanda Box reached 180,000 units.

This number was not bad, but then Chen Tianqiao made another bizarre move: only accepting full payment for pre-orders.

No one knew where he got that confidence.

At the end of last year, to increase its liquid capital, Shanda even sold off a large portion of its Sina shares. Even so, Shanda remained Sina's largest shareholder.

Li Yu, Vice President of Shanda's gaming division, said, "We can drop the talks for distributing 'DNF.' The game's quality is much worse than 'Future Era,' and the Korean side refuses to budge. Who knows when we'll ever reach an agreement."

"I think the company should focus on in-house development and supplement with distribution in the future," Zhang Xiangdong proposed.

He was also a vice president of the gaming division, but he was also in charge of Shanda's in-house game development.

"I agree," Chen Xiaodi immediately voiced his support.

As Shanda's second-largest shareholder, Chen Xiaodi also made it onto the "Forbes China Rich List" last year.

Chen Xiaodi continued, "Korean games are just so-so. Can't Chinese people make good games? Game Science is just a small company, yet they managed to make 'Future Era.' We can do it too. I led the acquisition of Qidian, and there are many novels there that can be adapted into games."

Shanda did indeed spend that year heavily publicizing that it would focus on in-house development in the future.

However, their approach was not to develop games internally. Instead, they acquired a large number of small and medium-sized game companies, especially those that had already achieved some success.

After acquiring them, they all went under...

"I'll think about it," Chen Tianqiao did not agree immediately, but he did issue an order, "Terminate the 'DNF' distribution negotiations with the Korean side."

Shanda, Tencent, and several other Chinese companies all terminated their negotiations with the Korean developer, Neople.

Neople's founder, Heo Min, slammed his desk in anger.

The man wore a pair of black round-rimmed glasses, and his hair fell to his shoulders, making him look somewhat like an artist.

It was Heo Min himself who had instructed the Korean side to repeatedly go back on their word and raise the price during negotiations. He had carefully studied the Chinese online game market and believed he had the Chinese game companies in the palm of his hand.

After his fit of rage, Heo Min gradually calmed down and analyzed the situation seriously, "If one company terminates negotiations, it could be due to their own internal decisions. But for all of them to terminate negotiations, something must have happened on the Chinese side. What exactly happened in China?"

The executive in charge of overseas markets said, "Our negotiation representative stationed in China said over the phone that a Chinese company has launched a new game. That new game's core gameplay is almost identical to 'DNF.'"

Heo Min, who had just calmed down, flared up again upon hearing this. "The Chinese must be copying us. I'm going to sue them!"

The executive said, "We can't sue. The game's world-building, story, and art are all different from our 'DNF.' Identical core gameplay doesn't constitute infringement. This is different from Shanda imitating 'The Legend of Mir' to make 'The World of Legend.'"

Heo Min said, "Have the negotiation representative re-establish contact with the Chinese companies. Tell them we are willing to lower the distribution fee and revenue share. Moreover, our Korean game is more fun and has more market potential than the Chinese imitator."

The executive said hesitantly, "The representative said that based on the opening and cutscene animations released by the Chinese company, as well as the gameplay screenshots uploaded by the closed beta players, that Chinese game seems to have more refined graphics than ours. As for playability, that's not clear yet."

Heo Min said, "Have the representative buy a closed beta account and try out the Chinese game personally. Also, regardless of whether it constitutes infringement, we must sue them with great fanfare. Pay the Chinese media to publicize this and ruin that game's reputation, define it as a copycat! Even if we lose the lawsuit, Chinese players will look down on that game. Then it will be much easier to negotiate."

The executive offered a suggestion, "If we lose the lawsuit, we can continue to smear that game. We'll just say the Chinese government is protecting its own country's copycats, and we are the victims of plagiarism and suppression."

Heo Min was very satisfied with this, praising him, "You have a good head for business warfare."
